disposition_reason: Soil-only survey of 40 cacao plantation sites in four Peruvian Amazon regions; the authors state they did not measure Cd in cacao beans or plants, so there are no cocoa occurrence values. Soil Cd and site/management associations are recorded as observational context.
disposition_locator: Section 4.3, p.10 ('Although we did not measure Cd contents in the cacao beans or plants at our study sites')

study.growing_origin_vs_market: Peru: Madre de Dios (12 sites), Ucayali (8), Amazonas (13), San Martin (7)
study.sampling_unit: one composite of eight subsamples per 100 m2 site
study.method: EPA 3015A microwave HNO3 extraction; flame AAS (EPA 700 B:2007); pH 1:2.5 soil:water

controls.outcome: Soil Cd (not bean) 1.57 ± 0.47 mg/kg Madre de Dios, 1.67 ± 0.14 Ucayali, 1.92 ± 0.13 Amazonas, 2.46 ± 0.22 San Martin (p<0.001); range 1.1-3.2 mg/kg; soil Cd correlated with elevation r = 0.40 (p<0.05). Bean Cd not measured.

controls.control: Geological substrate / soil type (avoid alluvial deposits and Leptosols)
controls.comparator: Soil Cd across substrates and soil associations
controls.outcome: Soil Cd 2.69 ± 0.24 mg/kg on alluvial deposits vs 1.55 ± 0.04 on detritus/sand/gravel; Cretaceous 2.10 ± 0.18 and Paleo-Neo 2.14 ± 0.19 vs Quaternary 1.62 ± 0.06; Eutric Leptosol 2.46 ± 0.22 and Dystric Leptosol 2.14 ± 0.19 vs Dystric Gleysol 1.58 ± 0.10 (p<0.001). Soil only.
Soil pH (4.4-8.3) correlated positively with total soil Cd, r = 0.57 (p<0.05); association with bean Cd not assessed.

controls.control: Fertiliser use, management type, cacao variety, plantation age
controls.comparator: Sites with vs without fertilisers (Guano de Isla, Sulfomag, dolomite, phosphatic rock; MD and SM only), cut-deposit/compost/no-cut management, CCN51 (33 of 40 sites) vs other varieties
controls.outcome: No significant effect on soil Cd or soil pH (no effect sizes given); most plantations young (38 of 40 <=10 years).

regulatory.instrument: Regulation (EU) No 488/2014 (as described by the source)
Regulation (EU) No 488/2014 (as described by the source)

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Summary 'Implications' states EU 488/2014 thresholds of 600 ppb in beans and 800 ppb in powder; the primary says 0.6 mg/kg cacao powder and 0.8 mg/kg beans (reversed in the summary). Note the source's own 'beans' attribution is itself questionable: Reg. 488/2014 lists cocoa powder and chocolate categories, not raw beans (verify against the instrument).

Summary says 'Year of cultivation showed r = 0.56 (p<0.01) with pH (more recently planted fields more acidic)'; the primary text gives r = -0.56 while Table 2 prints 0.56**; the direction is internally inconsistent in the source and the summary's interpretation is not stated by the authors.
Summary mentions 'AAS (Perkin Elmer)'; the primary does not name the instrument manufacturer.
Summary says management factors were 'self-reported by farmers'; not stated in the primary.
Summary omits the regional soil means (1.57, 1.67, 1.92, 2.46 mg/kg).
unresolved: No bean, nib or product Cd measured; nothing to extract as occurrence.
Internal inconsistency: sign of the year-of-plantation vs pH correlation (text r = -0.56; Table 2 0.56**).
Text says 80% of samples were below 2 mg/kg citing 'Table 2', but Table 2 is a correlation matrix; per-site values are in Supplementary Table S1, which was not available.
No QA/CRM information reported for soil Cd.
